narrative:
On September 30, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 39.5%, addressing 1,169 of the 2,960 scheduled matters across 59 sitting judges. This represents a noticeable dip in daily clearance compared to preceding sessions, sliding below the 49.1% achieved on September 29, 45.5% on September 28, and 43.4% on September 25.

Bench-level throughput demonstrated significant variation. Justice S. Rachaiah in Court Hall 30 handled the highest individual volume, hearing 87 of 171 scheduled matters (50.9%), while Justice Sachin Shankar Magadum in Hall 15 heard 67 of 134 listed cases (50.0%). Justice Shivashankar Amarannavar delivered high efficiency in Court Hall 22, taking up 55 of 61 cases (90.2%) on his primary list. Conversely, heavy dockets constrained progress elsewhere, with Court Hall 34 under Justice K. V. Aravind hearing 9 of 129 scheduled matters (7.0%).

Procedural stage analysis highlighted bottlenecks in substantive proceedings. Orders formed the bulk of scheduled activity with 934 cases, but only converted at 43.8% (409 heard), dropping from the 56.2% rate achieved on September 29. Admission matters maintained a steady 45.0% hearing rate (324 of 720). In contrast, Final Hearings experienced substantial stagnation, converting only 19.7% of its 544 scheduled cases (107 heard), down considerably from 32.0% on September 29 and 28.0% on September 28.

Subject-matter distribution was heavily dominated by Writ Petitions (WP), which comprised nearly half the docket at 1,363 scheduled cases but cleared only 36.3% (495 heard), down from 47.9% the prior day. Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) saw 195 of 499 heard (39.1%), also trailing the 48.8% conversion rate logged on September 29. Conversely, select appellate lists saw stronger movement, notably Criminal Revision Petitions (CRL.RP) at 67.2% and Criminal Appeals (CRL.A) at 50.7%.
